chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from Ghiyāth ibn Kullūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Jaʿfar, from his father, that ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say:
If a chicken, or something like it, dies in the well, two or three buckets are drawn from it; and if it is a sheep or something similar, then nine or ten.

So it does not contradict what we have presented earlier, because this report is anomalous, while what we have presented earlier accords with all the reports. Also, if we act upon those reports, then we have also acted upon these reports because they are included within them; but if we act upon this report, we would need to discard those reports altogether. And because certainty of the removal of impurity is attained by acting upon those reports, whereas it is not attained by acting upon this report.

key_terms.الدَّجَاجَةُ: a chicken; the example used for a smaller dead animal falling into a well
key_terms.النَّجَاسَةِ: ritual impurity whose removal is the legal concern in this passage
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being discussed in the ruling of ritual purity
key_terms.الْعِلْمَ: certainty or sure knowledge attained regarding the removal of impurity
key_terms.دَلْوَانِ: two buckets drawn from the well
key_terms.شَاذٌّ: an anomalous report that departs from the more established body of narrations

ai.seo_question: How does al-Istibṣār treat an anomalous hadith about drawing water from a well after an animal dies in it?
ai.summary: This passage discusses legal rulings concerning ritual purity when dead animals fall into a well and the number of buckets that should be drawn out. It also presents a juristic method of preferring a broader and more widely corroborated set of hadith over a solitary anomalous report, especially where certainty regarding the removal of najasah is concerned.
